prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, two overlapping people remain about 1.5–2.5 m in front of the camera, near the center; the smaller person is slightly to the right and partly occluded by the taller person. The bright pavement occupies the near foreground, while the darker wall, doorway, curb, and upper walkway are farther away, revealing the sloped ground and curb boundary more clearly than RGB alone. In frames 4–5, the camera wearer’s hand and forearm enter from the lower center-left and appear within roughly 0.2–0.8 m, while the two people remain beyond the wearer’s immediate arm’s reach but within each other’s reach. Depth boundaries merge the two people, erase fine gaps between limbs, and assign inconsistent brightness to the wall and ground, so exact distances and person-to-person separation are unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The map consistently isolates the two central people about 1.5–2.5 m ahead, with the taller person left/behind and the smaller person right/front, their masks overlapping because they stand within roughly 0–0.5 m of each other. It also reveals partially visible people: a distant figure near the upper-left edge in frame 1, another cropped figure near the top in frame 4, and the camera wearer’s forearm entering from the lower-left in frame 5; the other central person remains partly occluded throughout. Across frames 1–3 the pair stay near center with little depth change, then shift toward the right as the camera or subjects turn, while the wearer’s arm extends close to them in frames 4–5. The masks make instance extent and occlusion clearer than RGB, but labels overlap, some limbs merge or disappear, background surfaces are omitted, and the small green region labeled “skateboard” is likely an unreliable classification.
descriptions.pose: The yellow skeleton places the main standing body roughly 1.5–2.5 m ahead and tracks its head above the torso, legs below, and arms clustered in front, while magenta hand keypoints show hands near waist height and later the camera wearer’s hand entering from the lower-left. The body is mostly frontal or slightly turned toward the camera in frames 1–4, but frame 5 shows a side-leaning profile facing toward the right; head keypoints are too coarse to establish gaze reliably. The skeleton indicates that the central people’s hands and bodies overlap within arm’s reach of one another, whereas the wearer’s hand approaches from outside the body skeleton and appears within roughly 0.3–1 m of the camera. Pose clarifies joint arrangement and turning that are hard to separate in RGB, but it largely misses the smaller person, loses occluded limbs, produces unstable head and hand shapes, and cannot represent the scene layout or dependable metric distances.
